section_title: Acids and Bases: The Lewis Definition

mcmurry_topic_scope.textbook: Organic Chemistry (10th Edition) by John McMurry (OpenStax)
mcmurry_topic_scope.chapter_title: Chapter 2: Polar Covalent Bonds; Acids and Bases
mcmurry_topic_scope.section_coverage: 2.11 Acids and Bases: The Lewis Definition
key_concepts_ingested: Curved arrow formalism in Lewis acid-base reactions (heterolytic electron flow from the base lone pair to the acid vacant orbital)
Non-protic Lewis acids (species without H+ such as BF3 and AlCl3)
Coordinate covalent (dative) bond formation and formal charge shifts

lewis_acid.definition: A Lewis acid is an electron-pair acceptor: a chemical species that accepts an electron pair from a Lewis base to form a new covalent bond.
lewis_acid.orbital_requirement: A Lewis acid must possess a vacant low-energy orbital (such as an empty unhybridized 2p orbital on boron in BF3, an empty 3p orbital on aluminum in AlCl3, the empty 1s orbital of H+, low-energy d orbitals, or an accessible LUMO/antibonding orbital).
lewis_acid.electronic_characteristics: Electron-deficient, electrophilic, non-protic (such as neutral BF3 and AlCl3) or protic (such as H+), often possessing an incomplete valence shell (e.g., 6 valence electrons in group 13 neutral compounds) or an accessible LUMO capable of accepting an incoming electron pair.

representative_examples.name: Boron trifluoride
representative_examples.vacant_orbital: empty unhybridized 2p orbital on sp2 boron (the LUMO)

representative_examples.name: Aluminum trichloride
representative_examples.vacant_orbital: empty unhybridized 3p orbital on sp2 aluminum (the LUMO)

representative_examples.name: Hydron (proton)
representative_examples.mass_basis: Bare proton: the neutral hydrogen atom mass minus one electron mass. The neutral atom value is listed under elemental_masses_mendeleev.
representative_examples.vacant_orbital: empty 1s orbital (the LUMO of the bare proton)

lewis_base.definition: A Lewis base is an electron-pair donor: a chemical species that donates a nonbonding electron pair (lone pair) to a Lewis acid to form a new covalent bond.
lewis_base.orbital_requirement: A Lewis base must possess a filled, high-energy nonbonding orbital (lone pair) or accessible electron density in a pi bond (HOMO).
lewis_base.electronic_characteristics: Electron-rich, nucleophilic, typically contains heteroatoms (O, N, S, P) with nonbonding electron pairs, as in ethers, amines, and water, or is a negatively charged anion or an electron-dense pi bond.

representative_examples.name: Dimethyl ether
representative_examples.donor_feature: two nonbonding lone pairs on sp3 oxygen

representative_examples.name: Water
representative_examples.donor_feature: two nonbonding lone pairs on sp3 oxygen

representative_examples.name: Trimethylamine
representative_examples.donor_feature: one nonbonding lone pair on sp3 nitrogen

representative_examples.name: Ammonia
representative_examples.donor_feature: one nonbonding lone pair on sp3 nitrogen

representative_examples.name: Hydroxide anion
representative_examples.donor_feature: three nonbonding lone pairs on anionic oxygen

adduct_formation_principles.bond_type: Coordinate covalent (dative) bond in which both bonding electrons originate solely from the Lewis base; the product is a Lewis acid-base adduct.
adduct_formation_principles.formal_charge_distribution: The donor atom experiences a formal charge change of +1 (losing sole ownership of the lone pair to share it), while the acceptor atom experiences a formal charge change of -1 (gaining shared ownership of the pair).
adduct_formation_principles.geometry_reorganization: Acceptor atom typically reorganizes hybridization and geometry (e.g., trigonal planar sp2 boron in BF3 reorganizes to tetrahedral sp3 in the BF3-ether adduct).

authentic_reactions.reaction_name: Boron trifluoride coordination with dimethyl ether
authentic_reactions.pedagogical_insight: Boron has a vacant 2p orbital; ether oxygen donates a lone pair into it to complete boron's octet, resulting in a dipolar complex.
Neutral trivalent boron accepts nitrogen's lone pair to form a stable 1:1 adduct with tetrahedral geometry at both B and N.

authentic_reactions.reaction_name: Aluminum trichloride coordination with chloride anion
authentic_reactions.pedagogical_insight: Trivalent aluminum expands from a 6-electron valence shell to a stable 8-electron octet by accepting a chloride lone pair.
Demonstrates that Bronsted-Lowry protonation is a specific subset of Lewis acid-base chemistry where H+ is the Lewis acid.

five_distractor_specification_matrix.choice_text: A chemical species that donates a proton (H+) via heterolytic cleavage of a polarized X-H bond.
five_distractor_specification_matrix.cognitive_failure_mode: Student fails to recall the broader electronic definition of acids and defaults to the familiar high-school / general-chemistry Brønsted-Lowry proton-donor paradigm, erroneously excluding non-protic Lewis acids like BF3 and AlCl3.
five_distractor_specification_matrix.pedagogical_refutation: Incorrect. Donating a proton (H+) defines a Brønsted-Lowry acid. Although the transferred proton (H+) itself is an electron-pair acceptor (Lewis acid), the parent molecule donating it is acting specifically as a Brønsted acid. The Lewis acid definition is fundamentally electronic and encompasses neutral, non-hydrogen species possessing vacant orbitals (e.g., BF3, AlCl3).
five_distractor_specification_matrix.mcmurry_10e_ground_truth_citation: McMurry 10e §2.11: Lewis acids are electron-pair acceptors; they are not restricted to species that contain or donate protons.

five_distractor_specification_matrix.choice_text: A chemical species that donates an unshared electron pair from a filled nonbonding orbital to form a coordinate covalent bond.
five_distractor_specification_matrix.cognitive_failure_mode: Student inverts the roles of donor and acceptor in memory recall, conflating the electron-pair donor (Lewis base/nucleophile) with the electron-pair acceptor (Lewis acid/electrophile).
five_distractor_specification_matrix.pedagogical_refutation: Incorrect. A chemical species that donates an electron pair is a Lewis base (nucleophile), not a Lewis acid. Lewis acids are electron-pair acceptors (electrophiles) that must possess a vacant low-energy orbital to accommodate the incoming electron pair.
five_distractor_specification_matrix.mcmurry_10e_ground_truth_citation: McMurry 10e §2.11: A Lewis base is an electron-pair donor; a Lewis acid is an electron-pair acceptor.

five_distractor_specification_matrix.choice_text: A chemical species that increases the concentration of hydroxide ions (OH-) when dissolved in an aqueous solvent medium.
five_distractor_specification_matrix.cognitive_failure_mode: Student confuses the modern general Lewis electronic definition with the historical, solvent-restricted 1884 Arrhenius definition of bases.
five_distractor_specification_matrix.pedagogical_refutation: Incorrect. Releasing hydroxide ions (OH-) in aqueous solution defines an Arrhenius base. The Lewis definition is universal across all media (gas phase, non-aqueous organic solvents, neat mixtures) and defines acid-base reactivity exclusively through electron-pair donation and acceptance.
five_distractor_specification_matrix.mcmurry_10e_ground_truth_citation: McMurry 10e §2.11: The Lewis definition transcends aqueous solutions and proton transfers, focusing strictly on electron-pair sharing.

five_distractor_specification_matrix.choice_text: A chemical species that donates an electron into a vacant orbital by undergoing spontaneous homolytic radical cleavage.
five_distractor_specification_matrix.cognitive_failure_mode: Student confuses heterolytic two-electron Lewis acid-base coordination with homolytic one-electron radical fragmentation.
five_distractor_specification_matrix.pedagogical_refutation: Incorrect. Lewis acid-base chemistry is strictly a two-electron (heterolytic) process involving electron pairs and double-barbed curved arrows. Radical reactions involve single electrons (homolytic cleavage) and fishhook arrows, which are fundamentally distinct from Lewis acid-base adduct formation.
five_distractor_specification_matrix.mcmurry_10e_ground_truth_citation: McMurry 10e §2.11: Lewis acid-base reactions involve curved arrows indicating the movement of a pair of electrons from a base to an acid.

five_distractor_specification_matrix.choice_text: Any chemical species bearing a net positive formal charge, such as the tetramethylammonium cation ((CH3)4N+), which attracts electron pairs regardless of octet occupancy.
five_distractor_specification_matrix.misconception_label: Charge-Valence Octet Fallacy (Cation = Lewis Acid Fallacy)
five_distractor_specification_matrix.cognitive_failure_mode: Student relies on a superficial heuristic that positive charge equates to acidity, failing to check whether the central atom possesses a vacant valence orbital or a completed octet.
five_distractor_specification_matrix.pedagogical_refutation: Incorrect. While many cations are Lewis acids (e.g., H+, carbocations), a positive charge does not guarantee Lewis acidity. Tetramethylammonium ((CH3)4N+) has a complete valence octet (8 valence electrons in four N-C bonds) and nitrogen lacks accessible low-energy d orbitals; it cannot accept an electron pair without violating the octet rule.
five_distractor_specification_matrix.mcmurry_10e_ground_truth_citation: McMurry 10e §2.11: To act as a Lewis acid, a species must possess a vacant low-energy orbital capable of accommodating an incoming electron pair.

pedagogical_misconceptions: Conflating Lewis acids with Brønsted acids (believing all acids must donate protons)
Inverting electron donor vs acceptor roles (confusing Lewis base with Lewis acid)
Restricting acid-base definitions to aqueous Arrhenius species (OH- and H3O+)
Confusing heterolytic two-electron pair donation with homolytic radical reactions
Assuming that all positively charged cations are Lewis acids regardless of octet saturation
